chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about salat (prayer) in the resting-places of camels and in the tethering-places of cattle and sheep. He said: If you sprinkle it with water and it is dry, then there is no harm in praying in them. But as for the tethering-places of horses and mules, then no.

key_terms.أَعْطَانِ الْإِبِلِ: the resting or watering places of camels
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer being discussed
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.مَرَابِطُ الْخَيْلِ وَالْبِغَالِ: the tethering places of horses and mules
key_terms.مَرَابِطِ الْبَقَرِ وَالْغَنَمِ: the tethering or keeping places of cattle and sheep
key_terms.نَضَحْتَهُ بِالْمَاءِ: you sprinkled it with water for cleansing

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) in places where animals are kept?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about performing salat (prayer) in places where certain animals are kept. It indicates permissibility in the places of camels, cattle, and sheep when sprinkled with water and dry, while excluding the tethering-places of horses and mules.
